note: Conformance vectors for the settler boundary. Omni runs these against its own
`Receipt::validate` in `tests/conformance.rs`; a settler written in another workspace
or another language should run the same file against its emitter, so both sides are
checked against one artefact rather than against each other's prose.
`accepted` is what omni does with the document, and nothing more. A vector that is
accepted is well-formed — it is NOT a statement that money moved. Nothing in this
contract can establish that, and the `fabricated-but-well-formed` case exists to make

vectors.name: settled
vectors.why: The ordinary success. A reference somebody can look up on a chain.

vectors.name: failed-with-a-reason
vectors.why: Definitely did not happen. Safe to retry, and the detail says why.

receipt.detail: counterparty returned 402 with requirements this settler cannot meet

vectors.name: settled-without-a-reference
vectors.why: The reference is the entire difference between a claim somebody can check and one they must take on trust. A settler that cannot produce one has not settled.

vectors.name: settled-with-whitespace-reference
vectors.why: Same rule. A blank that looks filled in is worse than an empty one.

vectors.name: failed-without-a-reason
vectors.why: An operator cannot tell whether to retry, which is the only decision a failure informs.

vectors.name: no-spend-record
vectors.why: A receipt about nothing in particular cannot resolve anything.

vectors.name: truncated-spend-record
vectors.why: Record ids are 16 hex characters. A short one is a truncation somewhere, and matching it loosely would let one receipt resolve the wrong spend.

vectors.name: fabricated-but-well-formed
vectors.why: ACCEPTED, and that is the point. This contract checks shape, never truth. A settler can lie and omni will take the document; the reference exists so a human or a chain lookup can catch it. Anything that reads `accepted: true` as proof of payment has misread the contract.

vectors.name: unnamed-settler
vectors.why: ACCEPTED. `settler` is optional so an operator can reconcile by hand from a block explorer without inventing a name for themselves. The reconciliation prints '(unnamed settler)' rather than implying provenance it does not have.

note: Values of `outcome` that must not parse at all, as distinct from parsing and failing
validation. A settler emitting one of these has misunderstood the contract, and the
failure should be loud at the boundary rather than becoming a quiet no-op.

cases.name: unknown
cases.why: A settler reporting 'I do not know' is reporting the state the record is already in. Accepting it would let reconciliation appear to make progress while changing nothing. A settler that cannot tell should emit NO receipt — silence is the honest signal, and the spend stays visibly unresolved.

cases.name: pending
cases.why: Same reason. 'Not yet' is not an outcome; come back when it is one.

cases.name: partial
cases.why: There is no partial settlement in this contract. A spend is one amount to one payee, and half of it is a different spend that was never authorised.
